Senses.PreferredTarget: having sought the mind, I could not find it
AlternateTargets: I sought the mind and found it altogether unobtainable
SearchAliases: I sought the mind but could not find it
Huike could not find the mind
Bodhidharma bring me your mind case
having sought the mind it was unobtainable
Senses.Explanation: Huike's fixed reply in the mind-settling case: ‘having sought the mind, I could not find it.’ The phrase occurs 121 times in 79 allowlisted texts. Huike says his mind is not at ease; Bodhidharma tells him to bring the mind so it can be set at ease; Huike answers with this phrase; Bodhidharma replies that the mind has now been set at ease. Subsequent records repeatedly examine the quoted sentence. Yuanwu asks why Huike answered only this. Juelang distinguishes Huike's utterance from later students repeating the same words. Zhuanyu Heng explicitly judges Huike's reply as falling into conceptual understanding when comparing it with the flower sermon, while Wanfeng asks how the sentence should be understood and comments on it in another register. Daxiu Zhu redeploys the wording in a first-person public question and is immediately asked where he is now. Huigong Xiong presses the abbreviated grammar: if it is altogether unobtainable, what remains to regulate? These disagreements and questions concern the force of one fixed quoted reply; they do not create a second referent.
Senses.Note: The Zen deviation is the promotion of one first-person reply into the fixed hinge of the lineage's mind-settling case. Six exact-headword witnesses span original-case transmission, public examination, criticism, later first-person reuse, and commentary. The shortened supporting quotation lacks the headword and is marked contrast. The critical appraisal is preserved rather than harmonized away. Huike and Bodhidharma remain on the lineage roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 磨曰。將心來。與汝安。祖曰。覓心了不可得。達磨云。與汝安心竟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Yuanwu Keqin's Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), Huike speaks the exact reply inside the bring-the-mind and mind-settling exchange; Bodhidharma responds, and Yuanwu is the later raiser and commentator.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只如二祖豈不會作許多道理。因甚麼只答道。覓心了不可得
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu Keqin, in the Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), asks why the Second Patriarch answered only ‘having sought the mind, I could not find it.’

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huigong Xiong, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huigong Xiong of Nanhai Baoxianglin (南海寶象林慧弓詗禪師語錄), presses the abbreviated wording by asking what remains to regulate if it is altogether unobtainable; this support lacks the headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又如達磨令神光將心為汝安，光覓心了不可得即為安心，今日學人亦曰：『我覓心了不可得。』我今曰：『為汝安心竟。』彼能如神光即頓悟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Juelang Daosheng, in the Complete Record of Chan Master Juelang Sheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄), contrasts Huike's utterance with later students repeating the same words and questions whether the same response follows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 磨云：『將心來，與汝安。』豈不涉於語言；光云：『覓心了不可得。』未免落於知解。較之釋迦拈花、迦葉微笑，豈不千里萬里去也？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Preceptor Zhuanyu Heng at Purple Bamboo Grove (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄), Zhuanyu explicitly quotes Huike speaking the exact reply, then judges it to fall into conceptual understanding when compared with the flower-sermon exchange. Huike is the token speaker; Zhuanyu is quoter, commentator, and record owner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 便進方丈問曰：『若人識得心，大地無寸土。某即今覓心了不可得，又識個甚麼心？』童云：『你即今在甚處？』遂頓足云：『在者裡。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Daxiu Zhu, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Daxiu Zhu (大休珠禪師語錄), recounts using the phrase in a first-person question and being asked where he is at that very moment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 神光踏發毒箭，射中泥牛，卻道覓心了不可得，和贓捉敗。磨云：『吾與汝安心竟』，血濺梵天。且道『覓心了不可得』如何話會？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wanfeng Zhishan, in the Recorded Sayings of Preceptor Wanfeng (萬峰和尚語錄), comments on Huike's exact words and publicly asks how the phrase should be understood.
